tasks.description:
**Question.** How far does internal drift bend the perceived path of a moving Gabor? Which physical path angle looks vertical?

**What is on the screen.** A black fixation dot. After gaze is held and a 400-600 ms foreperiod, a Gabor (sine carrier, Gaussian envelope) appears mid-path [[param:path_center_dva]] from fixation and moves back and forth along a [[param:path_length_dva]] straight path at [[param:path_speed_dva_s]]. Its stripes run along the path and drift across it at [[param:drift_tf_hz]], reversing with each pass.

**What the subject does.** Keeps fixating (eye tracker: leaving the window or blinking ends the trial and it is repeated) and presses the left or right arrow for whether the path looks tilted left or right of vertical.

**Varied.** The physical path angle, set by interleaved QUEST+ staircases ([[param:staircases_per_side]] per drift pairing); the drift pairing (the one that makes a right- or left-tilted path look vertical).

**Measured.** Left/right reports as a function of physical angle; the analysis fits the angle seen as vertical (PSE) per pairing.

**What it can and cannot show.** The size of the perceptual illusion for this observer, which sets the paths used in the saccade task. Only the physical path is on the screen; the perceived path is inferred from reports, never drawn.
notes: Example angle 49° is the paper's mean right-tilt PSE (configs/task.yaml); here the angle is adaptive.
ASSUMED (configs/task-perception.yaml): fixation colour/size/window, carrier phase, acquire 5 s / 100 ms, 500 ± 100 ms foreperiod, 500-ms interval, staircase counts and lengths, block layout.

Geometry rule: the stripes run along the physical path; the internal drift is perpendicular to the stripes (across the path) and reverses at each path reversal, in step with the envelope. Only the physical path exists; the perceived (illusory) path is never drawn.
Drift arrow shows the right-tilt pairing while the envelope moves up the path (drift to the left); it points the other way on the way down, and the left-tilt pairing is the mirror image.
Diagram background is the window's mid-grey (the paper's 5.3 cd/m² is documentation, not set by software). The 2-dva gaze window is drawn as a radius, as the code uses it.

Gabor drawn to scale with the renderer's sine carrier and Gaussian envelope: sigma 0.1 dva, 2 c/dva, patch radius 3 sigma (about 1.2 cycles across). Carrier phase is random per trial in the code; the drawing shows phase 0.

The drift arrow is drawn by the renderer normal to the stripes (drift 'backward' = against the wave vector = up and to the left), the right-tilt pairing while the envelope moves up the path; it reverses on the way down.

tasks.description:
**Question.** Do saccades go to where the moving Gabor is, or to where it is seen?

**What is on the screen.** A black fixation dot; after 400-600 ms the double-drift Gabor appears mid-path [[param:path_center_dva]] from fixation and moves back and forth along a path at [[param:path_angle_right_deg]] or [[param:path_angle_left_deg]] (the angles seen as vertical; group means shipped, set per participant). Half the trials are the no-drift control (same path, no internal drift).

**What the subject does.** Fixates until the dot goes off, at one of [[param:n_fix_off_times]] times over one motion cycle (0.75-3.25 s), then saccades to the Gabor. The Gabor is removed as soon as gaze leaves the window, so there is no visual feedback about the landing.

**Varied.** Path tilt (right or left pairing), internal drift (on or control), fixation-offset time.

**Measured.** Saccade landing positions; the analysis recovers the path orientation the landings follow (drift minus control) and the landing shift across the path.

**What it can and cannot show.** If landings follow the physical path, the saccade system does not use the accumulated perceptual shift (the paper's finding). Saccade onset and landing are detected online at the display rate, not by the paper's offline 1-kHz analysis; calibrate the tracker before every session.
notes: Offset times 0.75, 1.25, ... 3.25 s follow from the 3-dva path at 2 dva/s (geometry.fixation_offset_times).

ASSUMED (configs/task.yaml): start directions, carrier phase, acquire 5 s / 100 ms, 500 ± 100 ms foreperiod, 1-s saccade limit, landing rule (30 dva/s, 150 ms, 5-dva window, which does not gate the outcome), 500-ms interval, trials per condition.

Geometry rule: the stripes run along the physical path; the internal drift is perpendicular to the stripes (across the path) and reverses at each path reversal, in step with the envelope. Only the physical path exists; the perceived (illusory) path is never drawn.
Drift arrow shows the right-tilt pairing while the envelope moves up the path (drift to the left); it points the other way on the way down, and the left-tilt pairing is the mirror image.
Diagram background is the window's mid-grey (the paper's 5.3 cd/m² is documentation, not set by software). The 2-dva gaze window is drawn as a radius, as the code uses it.

Gabor drawn to scale with the renderer's sine carrier and Gaussian envelope: sigma 0.1 dva, 2 c/dva, patch radius 3 sigma (about 1.2 cycles across). Carrier phase is random per trial in the code; the drawing shows phase 0.

The drift arrow is drawn by the renderer normal to the stripes (drift 'backward' = against the wave vector = up and to the left), the right-tilt pairing while the envelope moves up the path; it reverses on the way down.
